milestone: Collection — Theme-Scoped, Deduplicated Asset Registry (Phase 3: Manage Collection screen + Builder-only delete)
slice: Implements Phase 3 of the approved Collection plan -- the Theme-scoped registry's own management screen, a new _renderCollectionPanel() mirroring _renderFramesPanel's own shape (a Scene-anchored bridge editor reached from the Phase-2 picker's new '🗂️ Manage Collection →' link, never a Global Navigation peer) but with no per-entry 'selected' detail state -- rename/availability/delete all fit inline on each row, since a Collection entry has far fewer fields than a Frame's eight. Wired into the existing modal-dispatch architecture exactly like Frames/Layer Packs/Assets already are (MODAL_NAVS/MODAL_TITLES/_renderContextPanel dispatch/STATE_GUIDANCE), and deliberately left OUT of WORKING_VIEW_PASSTHROUGH_NAVS since it has no Working View specimen of its own, matching Layer Packs/Assets' own precedent. Each row shows a real resolved thumbnail (_resolveAssetRefToSrc, reused unchanged from Phase 2), a rename text input (renameCollectionAsset), a live 'Used by N Experiences' count (collectionAssetUsageCount, already built in Phase 1 alongside renameCollectionAsset/setCollectionAssetAvailability -- Phase 1's own model-layer work already went further than its own phase name suggested, so Phase 3's real remaining work was purely this UI), a 'Let Creators use this too' checkbox (setCollectionAssetAvailability, reusing the existing _checkboxField helper verbatim), and a Delete button. Delete is gated behind a real window.confirm() naming the exact live usage count before committing ('It is currently used by N Experiences — those will lose this picture'), then calls the already-shipped deleteCollectionAsset (Phase 1) -- which nulls every Experience's imageSrc/graphicSrc currently pointing at the deleted entry through the real updateExperienceProperty path, so the Engine Adapter's own existing re-sync (_syncExperienceAttachments) fires and Working View/Runtime Preview both correctly clear rather than showing a stale image for a reference that no longer resolves to anything -- the exact AV-012 discipline already proven for Frame, now proven for Collection with two real, simultaneously-affected Experiences, not just one. An empty registry shows a real, non-crashing help message ('Nothing here yet...') rather than a blank panel. Verified via a comprehensive Playwright suite (25/25) driving the real UI end to end: the modal opens with the correct '🗂️ Collection' title reached via the real bridge link; two seeded Collection entries (one shared by two real Experiences, one genuinely unused) render with correct thumbnails/kind/live usage counts; rename and the availability checkbox both persist through their real model functions via real input/checkbox interactions; deleting the shared entry (behind a real, accepted confirm() dialog) nulls BOTH real Experiences' imageSrc in one operation while leaving the unrelated unused entry completely untouched, and the panel correctly re-renders down to one row; deleting the now-unused entry is confirmed a clean no-op elsewhere (zero entries left, nothing else in the project changed); the empty state renders correctly and the bridge link stays reachable with zero entries; and a static grep confirms Collection's delete/rename/availability functions are absent from every root Studio (Creator) JS file -- Creator has zero code path anywhere that can reach them, matching the plan's own 'builder can delete from collection but not creator.' Full regression: both goldenBuild.js suites (World Builder v1 and v2, 30/30 each) pass unchanged; the Phase 2 picker's own 28-assertion suite passes completely unchanged, confirming zero regression from adding the new bridge link and management screen. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; tools/world-builder/ (v1) and root Studio are completely untouched -- confined entirely to tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js and tools/world-builder-v2/css/world-builder.css. Phases 4 (compile-time dedup in builder.js -- where 'reduces data load' is actually realized), 5 (Creator-facing availability metadata in the compiled package), and 6 (Creator-side 'From This World' browsing UI) remain named, not-yet-started increments -- see /root/.claude/plans/witty-floating-thimble.md for the complete phased rollout.
